When execution reaches the ICMP_REDIRECT branch while sock_owned_by_user(sk) is true, the old code still passes skb and the same sk to dccp_do_redirect. Although bh_lock_sock(sk) was called earlier, the ownership check only increments a statistic and does not block the operation, so the function does not establish that redirection is processed only when the user does not own the socket. If redirection handling and user operations access shared mutable state, a concurrency conflict can result; the affected state and consequence cannot be determined from the supplied function.

Although bh_lock_sock(sk) was called earlier, the ownership check only increments a statistic and does not block the operation, so the function does not establish that redirection is processed only when the user does not own the socket. If redirection handling and user operations access shared mutable state, a concurrency conflict can result; the affected state and consequence cannot be determined from the supplied function.

Before dccp_do_redirect(skb,sk) in the ICMP_REDIRECT branch, after checks !sock_owned_by_user(sk). 适用前提.check_zh: 在目标代码中存在与样本类似的长度、计数、偏移或索引递减/相减；受影响对象、长度/偏移、可达路径应逐项匹配；不能仅凭同名函数匹配。
适用前提.observed_input_and_state:
The function first confirms that the stream has at least 4 bytes, reads type and length, and then uses (size_t)(*length - 4) directly as the remaining payload length for comparison. When *length is less than 4, this expression no longer represents a valid payload length. The original first check protects header reads only and does not guarantee that the declared length includes the header. This alone cannot establish that the old code accepts a short length or performs an out-of-bounds access: if the subtraction is negative, conversion to size_t usually produces a very large value, and the existing remaining-length check will usually reject it.
Type description under current review: insufficient lower-bound validation of the length field; boundary risk in subtraction and unsigned conversion

适用前提.observed_input_and_state:
When link support is enabled and the hard-link name is non-empty, before directly calls link with linkname as source and a->name as target. If the source path resolves to a file outside the permitted scope and link succeeds, it creates a hard link to that file; when a->filesize > 0, it then opens a->name with O_TRUNC and may truncate the same file. Existing non-null checks, link's return value, and the filesize condition constrain branch selection, link success, and opening only; they do not verify that the source path follows path and symlink policy. O_EXCL in the ordinary-file branch does not protect this early-return hard-link branch.
Type description under current review: insufficient validation of a hard-link source path, conditionally causing path escape and truncation of an associated file

classification.repair_pattern_zh: 写入/读取前的长度与实际容量约束

危险操作.mechanism_zh: 以不相符的长度执行数据操作
危险操作.original_context_sentence: When removing an internal /./, memmove's destination is cp and its source is cp + 2, but its length is the entire string's strlen(file) - 1.

适用前提.check_zh: 在目标代码中存在与样本类似的以不相符的长度执行数据操作；受影响对象、长度/偏移、可达路径应逐项匹配；不能仅凭同名函数匹配。
适用前提.observed_input_and_state:
When removing an internal /./, memmove's destination is cp and its source is cp + 2, but its length is the entire string's strlen(file) - 1. Let the current string length be L and cp's offset from file be d; the length required from the source to the terminator is L - d - 1, so the old code copies d extra bytes. When d > 0, it reads beyond the terminator; if the underlying object has insufficient space, an out-of-bounds read occurs, and the target range may also go out of bounds. strstr finding /./ guarantees only that a match exists, not that copying from an internal position using the whole-string length is safe; memmove's overlap support does not fix an excessive length.
Type description under current review: potential out-of-bounds read/write caused by using the wrong basis for copy length

漏洞触发条件.precise_case_mechanism:
When removing an internal /./, memmove's destination is cp and its source is cp + 2, but its length is the entire string's strlen(file) - 1. Let the current string length be L and cp's offset from file be d; the length required from the source to the terminator is L - d - 1, so the old code copies d extra bytes. When d > 0, it reads beyond the terminator; if the underlying object has insufficient space, an out-of-bounds read occurs, and the target range may also go out of bounds. strstr finding /./ guarantees only that a match exists, not that copying from an internal position using the whole-string length is safe; memmove's overlap support does not fix an excessive length.
Type description under current review: potential out-of-bounds read/write caused by using the wrong basis for copy length

The only change in the internal /./ branch changes the copy length from strlen(file) - 1 to strlen(cp) - 1. After locating cp, the length is computed from the suffix at that position; because the match guarantees that the suffix contains at least three characters, copying that length from cp + 2 includes exactly the original terminator and removes the extra bytes caused by the prefix offset.

适用前提.check_zh: 在目标代码中存在与样本类似的执行乘法、加法、长度或偏移运算；受影响对象、长度/偏移、可达路径应逐项匹配；不能仅凭同名函数匹配。
适用前提.observed_input_and_state:
before repeatedly left-shifts the Py_ssize_t new_size by one while seeking a power of two no smaller than min_size. If the next doubling exceeds the signed type's representable range, new_size <<= 1 has already produced undefined behavior. The loop condition new_size > 0 checks only the value before shifting, while a later new_size <= 0 relies on the post-overflow result; neither protects the shift that overflows. assert(min_size > 0) likewise does not constrain the upper bound of doubling.
Current review type: signed left-shift overflow during capacity doubling (undefined behavior)

安全反证.verification_goal_zh: 运算前做范围检查或扩大运算类型；检查后续缩窄转换
安全反证.repair_observed_not_proof_of_any_other_c:
after changes min_size, new_size, and to_process to size_t and rejects min_size > PY_SSIZE_T_MAX before doubling. It then computes capacity with unsigned new_size instead of relying on a signed shift overflowing into a nonpositive value. Provided size_t can represent the power-of-two ceiling for permitted requests, the loop finishes before wraparound; an oversized request returns before allocating the new table or modifying self state. On allocation failure, restoration of the old table, clearing of the new table, entry migration, and release of the old table remain unchanged.
Current review repair-mechanism description: when capacity grows by powers of two, constrain request upper bound before computing and use an unsigned type that can hold the rounded result; do not detect overflow through the sign change after signed overflow. The request bound must also ensure the rounding process itself does not wrap.

Before each of the seven reads that computes an index from the current cc.ccs, after first requires WC_CCS_INDEX(cc.ccs) >= WC_F_ISO_BASE. 适用前提.observed_input_and_state:
When the parser is in PARA_VALUE_QUOTED state and encounters a backslash, the old code directly reads *(tmp+1). The loop condition tmp < end protects only the current character and cannot guarantee that the next character exists; when tmp == end - 1, this read crosses the input interval. If end is the end pointer of the underlying object, this is a memory out-of-bounds read. In addition, after the loop is exhausted, even if the parser remains in a quoted-value state it enters endofheader without explicitly reporting an unclosed quote.
Current review type description: out-of-bounds read (CWE-125); improperly accepting an argument with an unclosed quote

If end is the end pointer of the underlying object, this is a memory out-of-bounds read. In addition, after the loop is exhausted, even if the parser remains in a quoted-value state it enters endofheader without explicitly reporting an unclosed quote.
Current review type description: out-of-bounds read (CWE-125); improperly accepting an argument with an unclosed quote

The backslash branch first checks tmp+1 == end and, when true, jumps to parse_error before the lookahead read and tmp++; tmp still points to the in-range backslash at that point. After natural loop termination, it separately checks PARA_VALUE_QUOTED and sends an unclosed quote to error handling. The added endofheader debug log does not change the boundary relationship. However, when the loop ends with tmp == end, the new error-path log still contains *tmp, leaving a boundary read issue.
Current review fix mechanism description: A loop boundary for the current character cannot replace the boundary check for a lookahead. First verify that the next character remains inside the input interval, then read and skip the escaped character; when input is exhausted, reject an incomplete structure according to parse state, and ensure error reporting also avoids dereferencing an end pointer.

Both paths round the name length up to an 8-byte boundary.
